title: De Fide. Spe Et Charitate
author: Augustine

passages.original: non itaque culpentur dispensatores fideles, non sua neglegentia uel pigritia, sed quorundam potius contumacia, qui pecuniam dominicam recusant accipere et adulterinam suam cogunt seruos dominicos erogare, dum nolunt saltem tales mali esse, quales sanctus Cyprianus commemorat, saeculo uerbis solis et non factis renuntiantes, quando nec uerbis renuntiare diaboli operibus uolunt, cum se in adulterio permansuros uoce apertissima profitentur. si quid ab eis dici solet, quod forte disputando non adtigi, tale arbitratus sum, cui mea responsio necessaria non fuisset, siue quod ad rem, de qua agitur.
passages.english: So let faithful stewards not be blamed, not for their own negligence or sloth, but rather the obstinacy of certain people, who refuse to accept the Lord's money and compel the Lord's servants to pay out their own counterfeit [coin], since they are unwilling to be even such bad men as Saint Cyprian mentions, renouncing the world in words alone and not in deeds, when they will not renounce the works of the devil even in words, since they declare in the plainest voice that they will remain in adultery. If anything is usually said by them that I perhaps did not touch on in my discussion, I judged it to be of such a kind that my reply to it would not have been necessary, either because [it did not bear] on the matter under discussion,
passages.notes: The passage ends mid-sentence; the clause is completed in the following context ("non pertineret, siue quod tam leue esset...": "did not bear on it, or because it was so trivial that anyone could very easily refute it"). The opening "non... non... sed" is awkward as transmitted: the sense is that blame lies not with the stewards' negligence but with others' obstinacy.
